prompt: Step 1: The attached image is an exact anatomical layout of a zoomed-in cross-section of the right groin at the inguinal crease, as seen under an ultrasound probe: skin at the top, medial on the left, lateral on the right. From the top down: a thin skin layer, a thick layer of yellow lobulated subcutaneous fat, a thin white fascia lata line, then deeper fat. On the left: a large oval blue femoral vein and, to its right, a round red femoral artery. A second thin white line, the fascia iliaca, runs across the middle of the image on top of the large dark-red iliopsoas muscle and turns down along the muscle's left edge. Just under that line, to the right of the artery: a flat yellow femoral nerve; further right under the line, a small round yellow nerve. On the upper right, a red sartorius muscle. At the very bottom, a pale bone surface. Repaint it as a premium medical-atlas illustration. Keep every structure exactly where it is, with the same size, outline and position; the image will be overlaid with exact markings afterwards, so nothing may move. Both white fascia lines must stay clearly visible as thin separate layers, and the muscle should show fine fibre texture. Change only the rendering: soft painted shading, fine crisp outlines, realistic skin, fat, muscle, vessel, nerve and bone textures, gentle depth and light from the upper left. Calm, restrained palette on the same off-white background. Do not add, remove, move or resize anything, and add no text, letters, numbers, labels, lines, arrows, needles, probes, instruments, hands or blood. Step 2: the 'Image 1 is the exact layout ... Image 2 is for understanding the anatomy only ...' prompt (visuals/ficb_anatomy_layers history, 2026-09-30), with the step-1 painting as image 1.
promptStep2:
Image 1 is the exact layout. Use it as the structure for a scientifically accurate cross-section of the right groin under a linear ultrasound probe, seen straight on as a cut face: keep every outline, position and size exactly as drawn, in the same 4:3 landscape frame, with the tissue running to all four edges. Exact labels and a needle will be laid over it afterwards.

Image 2 is for understanding the anatomy only: how the femoral nerve lies in the fascial plane beneath the fascia iliaca, on the surface of the iliopsoas, and how injected fluid opens that plane, lifting the fascia iliaca off the muscle and surrounding the nerve. Take the relationships from image 2; take every position, shape and size from image 1; the drawing itself is new.

Paint it as a premium regional-anaesthesia atlas plate: a rich, deep, saturated palette with soft glossy highlights, fine crisp outlines and gentle depth, lit softly from the upper left.

Work from the top down:
1. The grey probe rests on the skin and presses it into a shallow dent. The skin is a thin pink layer.
2. The subcutaneous fat is dense, small orange-gold lobules with fine pale septa and a soft sheen.
3. The fascia lata and the fascia iliaca are thin, crisp, glistening white-pink sheets.
4. Under the fascia iliaca, the opened fascial plane is a smooth, pale, glassy layer of fluid that lifts the fascia off the muscle and surrounds both nerves.
5. The femoral nerve lies inside that fluid layer: a flat olive-yellow oval in a thin pale sheath, divided into four large, finely speckled fascicle compartments. The small round nerve on the left lies in the same layer, drawn the same way with two compartments.
6. Below the fluid layer, the iliopsoas has its own thin pale fascia on its surface. The iliopsoas and sartorius are deep maroon muscle made of flattened fascicle bundles that overlap like scales, each edged with a thin white streak of connective tissue, with a few tiny paired red and blue vessels scattered through it.
7. The femoral artery has a thick, layered red wall around a dark lumen; the femoral vein has a thinner blue wall around a dark blue lumen.
8. Along the bottom, the bone has a smooth ivory cortex over pale spongy bone.

The picture shows only this anatomy and the probe.

selection: Owner, 2026-09-30: 'This was by far the nicest looking image' - the tissue quality (muscle, nerve, fat, vessels, fascia) beat every later attempt. An earlier review here wrongly said it was framed and shrunk; an overlay shows it lies on its reference within a few pixels (the pale strips are the space above the skin and the bone).
rejected: First layout (wide groin section, lateral left): owner rejected the composition and asked for the NYSORA-style zoomed plane. Painting of the flat-colour zoomed layout: framed and shrunk inside a border, nerves as angled cables, lengthwise muscle fibres, bubble fat. The owner judged it not good; the reference was given cut-face texture cues and the prompt rewritten from scratch. Muscle repair of the bf313d6 base ('angular polygons'): nerves ballooned into large bundles, valve leaflets in the vein, stray vessels in the muscle; rejected. The bf313d6 base itself was withdrawn for a new attempt after the owner shared a second gold-standard plate: layout rebuilt with flattened overlapping fascicle bundles, small intramuscular vessel pairs, a compartmented femoral nerve, orange-gold fat and the probe denting the skin. Later attempts from textured references (dotted and scale-pattern muscle, compartment nerves) copied the reference's crude texture; the owner judged their quality worse. Crop repaint to widen the probe: Gemini zoomed the whole crop about 1.2x, widened the probe to only half the field and kept the dent; not used.
knownLimits: A faint ripple remains in the skin's lower border where the dent's shoulders were. The code-drawn probe is a plain grey body. The muscle shows lengthwise fibres; Gemini curved the bone up under the lateral muscle. Light falls from the upper right after the mirror. Needle, entry, injectate, the plane's floor line and the probe are code-drawn.
edits: Dent flattened: the painted skin was pressed about 2.2 mm down under Gemini's 1.4 cm probe. A per-column vertical warp confined to the rows above the fascia lata (base rows <= 252) moved the skin surface to one level (base row 117) under the probe, easing back to its natural height across the lateral gap; the fat above the fascia lata takes the shift. Nothing at or below the fascia lata moved.

The probe is code-drawn across the whole field (owner, 2026-09-30: the section is the ultrasound plane, so the probe covers its whole top), ending just short of the lateral edge where the needle enters; it covers Gemini's narrow probe.
